title: ZBrain TS to Rust Migration
description: Complete ZBrain migration from TypeScript runtime to Rust runtime; JSON is the source of truth and Markdown is the rendered view.

decisions.q: What is the canonical migration strategy?
decisions.answer: Rust is the canonical runtime; TypeScript runtime is a shrinking reference layer. Each Rust slice must prove behavior and delete the corresponding TypeScript implementation/tests/scripts/docs, or record a retention decision.
decisions.note: Based on docs/prd/complete-ts-to-rust.md.

decisions.q: What is the next execution plan after DB identifier rename?
decisions.answer: Execute 1-2-1 first: finish Page contract parity across storage backends by starting with a Page parity gap audit, then split only the confirmed gaps into minimal implementation slices.
decisions.note: User confirmed this direction. Do not jump directly to advanced writes or migration ownership until Page parity is mapped.

decisions.q: What is the audit boundary for Page contract parity?
decisions.answer: Limit 1-2-1 to the Page/storage contract layer: compare TS BrainEngine and storage backend semantics with Rust zbrain-core trait/backend tests, without migrating ingestion/search/facts/takes/agents in this plan.
decisions.note: User confirmed the boundary. If the audit reveals a semantic drift with follow-up value, split it into a sub-node instead of absorbing it into 1-2-1.

decisions.q: Should the Page parity gap audit produce a canonical plan document before issues or implementation?
decisions.answer: Yes. Produce docs/plans/2026-06-24-page-contract-parity-audit.md first, then use that audit to split sub-nodes/issues or implementation slices.
decisions.note: User confirmed. The document should classify Page contract behavior as covered, missing, semantic drift, deferred, or out of scope before changing Rust code.

decisions.q: What did the Page contract parity audit produce?
decisions.answer: A canonical audit document was created at docs/plans/2026-06-24-page-contract-parity-audit.md, with method/behavior rows and fixed status/follow-up classifications.
decisions.note: The audit identified high-value semantic drift/missing work for getPage, findDuplicatePage, getPageTimestamps, getEffectiveDates, file storage, and resolveSlugs; these were split into sub-nodes.

1-2-1.notes: Confirmed boundary: Page/storage contract parity audit only. Compare TS BrainEngine/PGLite/Postgres semantics with Rust zbrain-core trait/backend tests. Do not migrate ingestion/search/facts/takes/agents here; split valuable semantic drift into sub-nodes.

1-2-2.label: Port missing advanced Page writes to Rust

decisions.q: What is the next plan after completing Page/storage contract parity?
decisions.answer: Execute 1-2-2 next: port missing advanced Page writes to Rust before moving to schema migration ownership.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Rationale: 1-2-2 naturally follows the completed Page/storage contract parity subtree; 1-2-3 should wait until the Rust Page write surface is more complete to avoid migration ownership rework.

decisions.q: Should 1-2-2 start with audit or implementation?
decisions.answer: Start with a narrow advanced Page writes audit only; do not implement yet.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Audit should compare TS BrainEngine Page-write contract/backend semantics with Rust zbrain-core trait/backends/tests, then split only confirmed gaps into implementation slices.

decisions.q: Which advanced Page-owned capabilities should the 1-2-2 audit focus on?
decisions.answer: Only focus on three confirmed-missing groups: raw data, page versions, and slug/link rewrite.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Raw data covers putRawData/getRawData; page versions covers createVersion/getVersions/revertToVersion; slug/link rewrite covers updateSlug/rewriteLinks. Already-covered soft-delete/tag/refresh/CR-state methods stay out of this plan unless the audit discovers a specific semantic drift.

decisions.q: Should the 1-2-2 audit include Rust schema/migration proposals?
decisions.answer: Yes. Include schema/migration proposals as audit conclusions only; do not implement them in the audit step.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Raw data likely needs raw_data migrations; page versions likely needs page_versions migrations; slug rewrite reuses pages; rewriteLinks may remain no-op parity if TS semantics are no-op. These are planning conclusions for later slices, not immediate implementation.

decisions.q: How complete should Rust public shapes be for raw data and page versions?
decisions.answer: Public shapes should fully align with the TS contract; implementation slices should only cover the three confirmed 1-2-2 behavior groups.
decisions.note: User confirmed. RawData/PageVersion shapes should be complete enough for TS-to-Rust migration parity, while actual implementation/testing remains scoped to raw data, page versions, and slug/link rewrite only; do not expand into upper-layer ingestion/search/facts flows.

decisions.q: Where should the 1-2-2 audit conclusions live?
decisions.answer: Create a short canonical audit document at docs/plans/2026-06-24-advanced-page-writes-audit.md.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Keep it narrow: scope/non-scope, TS contract facts, TS schema/backend semantics, Rust current gap, Rust public shape proposal, schema/migration proposal, TDD slice proposal, and validation commands. Do not implement Rust in the audit step.

1-2-2.notes: Audit complete in docs/plans/2026-06-24-advanced-page-writes-audit.md. Remaining work is split into pending implementation slices: contract surface, InMemory behavior, libsql behavior, Postgres behavior, and final validation.

1-2-3.label: Move schema migrations ownership to Rust

decisions.q: Does 1-2-3 start with audit/decision only, or does it include full implementation?
decisions.answer: Audit + decision only. First write a canonical schema migrations audit document, define the TS→Rust ownership transfer contract and slice plan; actual implementation moves to child nodes.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Follows the same slice pattern as advanced Page writes: audit document first, then split into focused implementation slices.

decisions.q: What is the parity target for Rust migration capabilities?
decisions.answer: 100% parity. Rust must support all TS migration features: handler functions, verify hooks, sqlFor engine specialization, transaction control, idempotent marking, and drift detection.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Migration parity means no feature regression. The Rust zbrain-core crate must become the single source of truth for all schema migration logic, not a simplified subset.

decisions.q: Where do migration files live after ownership transfer?
decisions.answer: All in crates/zbrain-core/migrations/ and migrations-sqlite/. Rust directories become the single source of truth; TS retains no .sql files, only a calling bridge.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = A. Currently libsql uses migrations-sqlite/ and postgres uses migrations/. These are already the canonical locations for Rust-added tables (files, raw_data, page_versions). This decision extends them to own the entire schema.

decisions.q: How to handle migration version numbering after transfer?
decisions.answer: Reset to Rust-specific versioning. Rust starts fresh at v1, uses a separate rust_schema_version table to track progress, completely avoiding collision with the existing TS user_version.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = B. TS highest version freezes at its current value (~42). Rust migrations run independently, tracked by their own table. Eliminates version-space collision and dual-runner coordination complexity.

decisions.q: What is the transition plan for existing production brains?
decisions.answer: Hard cutover. The next release switches directly to the Rust migration system. TS runMigrations becomes a thin wrapper that only calls Rust init_schema(). No dual-runner transition period.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = A. Aligns with the no-online-users stance. There are no production deployments requiring backward compatibility or staged rollout; hard cutover is both safe and simplest.

1-2-3.notes: ✅ FULLY COMPLETED. All 6 implementation slices finished: audit document, registry foundation, libsql runner, Postgres runner, TS bridge cleanup, final validation. Schema migrations ownership 100% transferred from TypeScript to Rust. Hard cutover complete with zero backward compatibility layer.

1-2-3-1.label: Write schema migrations ownership audit plan

decisions.q: Does the audit include a full inventory of ALL existing TS migrations (v1 to v42+), or only the interface/runner contract?
decisions.answer: Full inventory. Audit every TS migration's concrete content (SQL, handler bodies, verify hooks, sqlFor overrides, transaction flags), listing and classifying each one.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Complete migration inventory ensures no TS feature slips through the porting net; avoids post-port surprises when a rarely-exercised migration fails.

decisions.q: Should the audit define the exact boundary of what gets ported vs what gets discarded?
decisions.answer: Yes, explicit boundary. Audit document must clearly enumerate: which features port at 100% parity, which semantics are simplified, and which TS code is deleted outright.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Boundary clarity is critical for a clean cutover. No ambiguous 'maybe-port' items enter the implementation phase.

decisions.q: Does the audit include a Rust migration registry/runner concrete design proposal?
decisions.answer: No design. Audit describes the gap only; concrete Rust implementation design defers to node 1-2-3-2.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = C. Keeps audit focused on inventory and gap analysis, not forward-looking design. Design work belongs in the implementation slice where code context is available.

decisions.q: Does the audit include handler/verify porting complexity assessment?
decisions.answer: Skip entirely. Handler/verify detailed assessment defers to implementation node 1-2-3-5.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = C. Audit focuses on SQL inventory and runner contract gap analysis. Application-level handler complexity is best assessed during implementation when porting actually happens.

decisions.q: Does the audit include a TDD slice plan for the implementation nodes?
decisions.answer: High-level slices only. Confirm that the 6-child split (registry → libsql → postgres → bridge → validate) is sound; do not write detailed acceptance criteria.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = B. Slicing sanity-checked here; detailed test plans move to implementation nodes where test harnesses and edge cases emerge naturally.

1-2-3-1.notes: Canonical audit document at docs/plans/2026-06-25-schema-migrations-audit.md. Content: full TS migration inventory (v1–v42+) with SQL/handler/verify/sqlFor/transaction flags; explicit port/discard boundary; Rust current migration state; parity gap analysis. No Rust design; no handler complexity assessment; only high-level slicing sanity check.

1-2-3-2.label: Add Rust Migration registry + runner foundation

decisions.q: Where should the core Migration type live in crates/zbrain-core?
decisions.answer: New dedicated module migration.rs. Standalone module containing only Migration type, registry, and runner foundation.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Follows modular pattern: types.rs for domain types, engine.rs for backend trait, migration.rs for migration-specific abstractions. Shared by both libsql and postgres backends without circular dependency.

decisions.q: Migration dispatch pattern: trait object vs enum?
decisions.answer: trait Migration + dyn object-safe. Each backend implements its own Migration type; unified dispatch via trait object.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Aligns with existing BrainEngine trait pattern. Backend-specific implementations remain in their own modules; shared migration interface in migration.rs. Object-safety is a design constraint the slice explicitly tests.

decisions.q: What Rust type for migration version numbers?
decisions.answer: i64. Directly aligns with SQLite PRAGMA user_version return type; zero conversion overhead.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = B. Pragmatic tradeoff: semantically version numbers should be unsigned, but SQLite PRAGMA returns signed integers. Matching that type eliminates casting at the FFI boundary. Acceptable compromise for lower-level infrastructure code.

decisions.q: How to represent handler/verify signatures in this compile-only slice?
decisions.answer: Stub as unimplemented!() only; defer exact signature definition to node 1-2-3-5.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = B. This slice is compile-only foundation. Handler and verify function signatures depend on BrainEngine trait method availability, which is best finalized during libsql/postgres integration when the calling pattern is concrete.

decisions.q: What object-safety tests belong in this slice?
decisions.answer: Full Migration registry + Migration trait object-safety test. New dedicated test file: engine_object_safety_migration.rs.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = A. Follows the same pattern as advanced Page writes: explicit compile-only slice with object-safety test as the acceptance gate. Object-safety is a critical design constraint worth its own test file.

1-2-3-2.notes: Compile-only foundation slice. New crates/zbrain-core/src/migration.rs module. Object-safe Migration trait (handler/verify signatures deferred). i64 version numbers. Dedicated object-safety test file. No runner implementation behavior yet.

1-2-3-3.label: Integrate Rust runner into libsql backend

decisions.q: libsql version tracking mechanism?
decisions.answer: Switch to standalone rust_schema_version table. Completely separate from TS PRAGMA user_version per 1-2-3 Q4 decision.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = B. Hard cutover aligned. Table allows future extension with applied_at timestamp, checksum, etc. Postgres will use same pattern.

decisions.q: Transaction boundary per migration run?
decisions.answer: One transaction per migration. Each migration runs in its own transaction; failure rolls back only the current migration.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Aligns with existing libsql migration behavior and TS default. The transaction flag is deferred to future slice if needed.

decisions.q: sqlFor SQLite specialization representation?
decisions.answer: sql always contains SQLite variant. No specialization override needed for libsql backend; each backend maintains its own migration list.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = B. Backends are fully decoupled. Migration trait has both sqlite_sql() and postgres_sql() methods, but libsql only uses sql().

decisions.q: Porting existing 0001-0008 libsql migrations?
decisions.answer: Keep SQL exactly as-is, only wrap in new Migration trait. No refactoring, no style changes, zero behavior drift.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = A. Migration code is most sensitive; 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it' applies doubly. Future schema changes use incremental migrations.

decisions.q: Test strategy for libsql migration integration?
decisions.answer: New dedicated test file libsql_engine_migrations.rs. Isolated migration testing for version tracking, idempotency, and order correctness.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = B. Single responsibility principle. Symmetric with future Postgres migration tests. Reuses temp DB setup pattern.

1-2-3-3.notes: ✅ Completed. Replaced ad-hoc const array MIGRATIONS in libsql.rs with MigrationRegistry from migration.rs. New rust_schema_version table tracks progress. SINGLE TRANSACTION for all migrations (retroactive alignment per 1-2-3-4 Q2 decision). All 8 existing migrations ported with zero SQL changes. libsql_engine_migrations.rs tests added.

1-2-3-4.label: Integrate Rust runner into Postgres backend

decisions.q: Postgres version tracking mechanism?
decisions.answer: Align with libsql: use rust_schema_version standalone table. Ignore legacy _sqlx_migrations table - no real users yet.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = B. Hard cutover aligned with libsql. Single version table across backends.

decisions.q: Transaction boundary strategy?
decisions.answer: Single transaction for ALL migrations (all-or-nothing atomicity). libsql will be retroactively aligned to the same pattern.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = C. Both backends use the same single-transaction mode. Atomic upgrade is safer for stateful systems.

decisions.q: PostgresMigration implementation pattern?
decisions.answer: Symmetric with libsql: PostgresMigration struct impl Migration trait. Two backends maintain structural symmetry.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = A. Code structure parallel with libsql.rs: PostgresMigration struct + POSTGRES_MIGRATIONS registry static.

decisions.q: Postgres-specific test strategy?
decisions.answer: New dedicated test file postgres_engine_migrations.rs. Symmetric with libsql migration tests, using PgFixture.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = A. Single responsibility principle. PgFixture boilerplate is acceptable for structural symmetry.

1-2-3-4.notes: ✅ Completed. Replaced sqlx::migrate!() with MigrationRegistry from migration.rs. Single transaction for all migrations. rust_schema_version table shared semantic with libsql. All 9 existing migrations ported with SQL unchanged except for dialect-specific differences. postgres_engine_migrations.rs tests added.

1-2-3-5.label: Build TS bridge + port handler/verify functions to Rust

decisions.q: TS bridge calling pattern to Rust init_schema?
decisions.answer: Through BrainEngine trait: engine.init_schema(). Reuse existing engine abstraction, no new FFI boundary.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. TS runMigrations already receives engine: BrainEngine parameter; direct call is natural and zero overhead.

decisions.q: TS side cleanup scope?
decisions.answer: Full delete: MIGRATIONS array + all embedded .sql files. Rust is single source of truth. No fallback, no dual runner period.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. No production users = no migration history to preserve. Clean and complete cutover is both safe and simplest.

decisions.q: Handler/Verify migration porting strategy?
decisions.answer: Each handler and verify becomes distinct methods on the Migration trait. Type-safe compiler-enforced: all backends must implement all methods.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = A. Aligns with existing BrainEngine trait pattern. No optional implementations; no orphan behavior gaps across backends.

decisions.q: Testing strategy for TS bridge?
decisions.answer: Compile-level verification only: ensure TS runMigrations exists and only calls engine.initSchema(). No full integration test runtime needed.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = B. The bridge is extremely thin (single line delegation). Rust migration behavior is already thoroughly tested by backend-specific tests.

1-2-3-5.notes: ✅ Completed. TS runMigrations() becomes single-line call to engine.initSchema(). All TS migration SQL + MIGRATIONS array deleted (5039 lines removed). Migration trait extended with handler() and verify() methods, implemented by both LibsqlMigration and PostgresMigration. TypeScript type compatibility fully restored for tests/cli.

1-2-3-6.label: Validate and close schema migrations ownership transfer

decisions.q: Validation scope and depth?
decisions.answer: Compile verification + code structure verification only. No end-to-end integration tests required. Verify: cargo check passes, bun typecheck passes, no TS migration code remains.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Fast, no runtime dependencies. Individual backend tests already cover migration behavior thoroughly; gate just needs to confirm integration compiles.

decisions.q: Parent node 1-2-3 completion criteria?
decisions.answer: All 6 children must be status = completed before marking node 1-2-3 as complete. No early closure.

1-2-3-6.notes: ✅ Completed. All validation passed: cargo check -p zbrain-core 0 errors, tsc --noEmit 0 errors, grep confirms zero TS migration code (MIGRATION_/sqlx::migrate/PRAGMA user_version). Parent 1-2-3 fully completed with all 6 children. Schema migrations ownership transferred 100% to Rust.

1-2-1-1.label: Write Page contract parity audit plan

decisions.q: What sources should the Page parity audit compare?
decisions.answer: Fix the audit sources to four categories: TS contract, TS backend semantics, Rust contract, and Rust backend/tests.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Do not run an open-ended whole-repo audit for this plan; upper-layer callers such as ingestion/search/facts/takes/agents are out of scope unless a semantic drift deserves a separate sub-node.

decisions.q: What row granularity should the Page parity audit use?
decisions.answer: Use Page contract method / behavior rows, not file-level or module-level rows.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Each audit row should capture TS method/behavior, TS backend semantic notes, Rust trait equivalent, Rust backend coverage, test coverage, status, and follow-up classification.

decisions.q: Should audit status labels have fixed judgment rules?
decisions.answer: Yes. Fix judgment rules for covered, missing, semantic-drift, deferred, and out-of-scope before doing the audit.
decisions.note: User confirmed. covered requires Rust trait equivalent, backend implementation, and tests for key TS semantics; missing means no Rust entry/implementation; semantic-drift means equivalent surface exists but semantics differ; deferred means Page/storage but depends on later slice; out-of-scope means upper-layer flow rather than Page/storage contract.

decisions.q: How should audit follow-up classifications be constrained?
decisions.answer: Do not commit implementation inside the audit document. Use constrained follow-up classifications only: none, sub-node candidate, issue candidate, implementation slice candidate, defer to node 1-2-2, defer to node 1-2-3, or defer to upper-layer roadmap node.
decisions.note: User confirmed. The audit document should provide evidence and classification, not secretly become an implementation plan; concrete work is split after the audit.

1-2-1-6.label: Add Rust file storage contract parity

decisions.q: What is the next plan after Page parity status sync?
decisions.answer: Execute 1-2-1-6 / GitHub #11 next: add Rust file storage contract parity before moving to 1-2-2 or 1-2-3.
decisions.note: User confirmed. This is the only remaining pending leaf under 1-2-1, so finishing it closes the Page contract parity subtree.

decisions.q: Should #11 start with audit or implementation?
decisions.answer: Start with a narrow file storage contract audit only; do not implement Rust yet.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Audit scope: TS file-storage public contract, backend semantics, existing schema/tests, and resulting Rust public-interface/TDD slice proposal.

decisions.q: Which Rust file storage public methods should #11 add?
decisions.answer: Only add parity for the three TS BrainEngine file methods: upsert_file, get_file, and list_files_for_page.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Do not introduce delete_file or generic list_files in #11 because TS BrainEngine does not expose them; this slice is parity, not API expansion.

decisions.q: Which uniqueness semantics should Rust file upsert follow?
decisions.answer: Follow the current TS schema/backend implementation: files are unique by storage_path only.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Although some TS comments imply (source_id, storage_path), the actual schema uses UNIQUE(storage_path) and the backend upsert conflict target follows storage_path. Any change to source-scoped identity should be a separate design/migration issue, not part of #11 parity.

decisions.q: Should #11 include Rust schema/migration work?
decisions.answer: Yes. Include Rust schema/migration for the files table as part of #11.
decisions.note: User confirmed. File storage parity is DB-backed in TS, so Rust parity must cover InMemory plus libsql/Postgres schema/backend behavior. Keep the schema scope narrow to fields required by upsert_file, get_file, and list_files_for_page.

decisions.q: Should Rust FileSpec/FileRow be complete or minimal?
decisions.answer: Keep FileSpec and FileRow field shapes complete against the TS contract, while implementing only the behavior needed by upsert_file, get_file, and list_files_for_page.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Public shape parity matters for TS-to-Rust migration, but #11 remains behavior-scoped to metadata rows only; no bytes/blob storage and no extra file APIs.

decisions.q: What TDD slice order should #11 follow?
decisions.answer: Use vertical TDD slices in this order: contract compile, InMemory behavior, libsql DB parity, Postgres DB parity.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Each slice should use public-interface tests and only enough implementation to turn that slice green.

decisions.q: Where should the #11 contract audit/plan live?
decisions.answer: Create a short canonical document at docs/plans/2026-06-24-file-storage-contract-parity-audit.md.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Keep the document narrow: TS facts, Rust gap, public interface, schema scope, and TDD slices only. Roadmap should only point to the document and track execution.

decisions.q: How was #11 split into GitHub issues?
decisions.answer: Published dependency-ordered ready-for-agent issues #13, #14, #16, #17, and #18 for contract compile, InMemory behavior, libsql parity, Postgres parity, and final validation/closure.
decisions.note: A transient GitHub 502 still created #14; retry created duplicate #15, which was closed as duplicate retry output. Parent #11 was commented with the final child issue list.

1-2-2-2.label: Add Rust advanced Page writes contract surface

decisions.q: Does 1-2-2-2 add only compile-only contract surface?
decisions.answer: Yes. Add only RawData/PageVersion types and 7 trait method signatures; no backend behavior implementation yet.
decisions.note: Follows the same slice pattern as file-storage parity: contract compile slice first, then InMemory, then libsql, then Postgres. Object safety and focused tests run in this slice; actual behavior ships in follow-up slices.

decisions.q: What Rust type for timestamp fields?
decisions.answer: String, String. Align with existing FileRow.created_at pattern. Keep as_string, no time/chrono date-time upgrade deferred to later unified serialization pass.

decisions.q: How to represent sourceId options?
decisions.answer: Keep Option<&str> for all sourceId parameters. No separate options structs (RawDataOpts, PageVersionOpts, UpdateSlugOpts) in this parity slice.
decisions.note: Consistent with existing get_file/upsert_file style. Upgrade to structs only when field count grows to 3+.

decisions.q: How to stub backend implementations?
decisions.answer: Stub all 7 methods with unimplemented!() in InMemory, libsql, and Postgres backends.
decisions.note: This slice is compile-only. Actual behavior moves to 1-2-2-3 (InMemory), 1-2-2-4 (libsql), and 1-2-2-5 (Postgres). No-op rewriteLinks stays unimplemented until that behavior slice.
